D010_l001.question:
A 43-year-old divorced female private tutor presents with episodic mood disturbance characterized by distinct manic and depressive phases associated with marked functional impairment.

Over the past 1 month, she has exhibited a sustained period of markedly elevated irritability with pronounced psychomotor agitation, described as an inability to remain still or relax. Speech has been notably pressured, loud, and difficult to interrupt. She reports racing, intrusive thoughts that she cannot slow, with markedly reduced capacity to sustain attention on tasks. During this same period, she has experienced recurrent gustatory hallucinations, describing vivid tastes in the absence of any ingestion; these phenomena are temporally confined to the manic state and do not occur outside of it.

Preceding this, over approximately 4 months, she experienced a depressive episode characterized by pervasive loss of interest in usual activities, significant unintentional weight loss (>5% in one month), difficulty initiating sleep, and marked psychomotor slowing evident in delayed verbal responses. She reports low energy interfering with daily functioning and intense, irrational guilt regarding unrelated adverse events, reaching delusional intensity. She also describes sudden, intrusive urges to harm herself (e.g., jumping from heights or into traffic) without specific planning.
D010_l001.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Bipolar I Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D010_l001.answer: A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D010_l002.question:
A 29-year-old single male sound engineer presents with episodic mood disturbance characterized by distinct manic and depressive phases over the past several months, associated with marked functional impairment.

Approximately 5 months ago, he developed a depressive episode lasting about 4 months, marked by diminished interest in personal achievements, daily reduction in appetite, non-restorative but adequate-duration sleep, pronounced psychomotor slowing, pervasive low energy limiting daily activities, and persistent feelings of worthlessness. He reports recurrent, intense impulses to harm himself (e.g., by jumping from heights or into traffic) without a sustained plan or preparation.

Following this, he experienced a 1-month period of markedly elevated and euphoric mood accompanied by increased activity and inability to remain at rest. During this time, he demonstrated excessive and pressured speech, subjective acceleration of thought processes with rapid shifts between ideas, and heightened distractibility with attention captured by minor environmental stimuli such as sounds or movements. Visual hallucinations of people or objects were reported exclusively during this elevated mood period. Both mood phases led to significant impairment in occupational functioning and daily role performance.
D010_l002.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Bipolar I Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D010_l002.answer: A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D010_l003.question:
A 68-year-old married retired civil servant presents with a history of episodic mood disturbance. For approximately 1 month, he has exhibited marked mood lability, alternating between elevated and irritable states, accompanied by pronounced psychomotor agitation. He demonstrates pressured, incessant speech and reports an inability to slow or organize his thoughts, with markedly impaired concentration and difficulty maintaining attention on tasks. During this same period, he describes tactile perceptual experiences of being touched or movement on the skin without external stimulus, occurring exclusively in the context of the elevated mood state. This episode has led to significant social and occupational functional impairment within the home environment.

Over the past 4 months, he has also experienced a distinct period of pervasive loss of interest and inability to experience pleasure, associated with more than 5% weight gain over 1 month, initial insomnia, and low energy limiting routine activities. Psychomotor activity is notably slowed, particularly evident as delayed and reduced speech. He reports excessive, irrational guilt of delusional intensity regarding unrelated adverse events and has engaged in a suicide attempt, indicating high risk and substantial functional impairment during this depressive phase.
D010_l003.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Bipolar I Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D010_l003.answer: A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D010_l004.question:

During this same period, he reported tactile hallucinations, describing abnormal sensations on his skin in the absence of external stimulus. Subsequently, over about 4 months, he developed a depressive episode with marked social withdrawal, prominent physical fatigue, and significant unintentional weight loss (>5% body weight in 1 month).     D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D010_l005.question:

Speech during this time was markedly accelerated and difficult to interrupt, driven by an internal sense of pressure. He described a rapid, disorganized flow of ideas with multiple thoughts occurring simultaneously and reported being easily drawn to minor environmental stimuli, frequently shifting focus to trivial noises or movements. During this same period, he reported recurrent visual perceptual experiences of seeing people and objects that were not present. These perceptual disturbances have occurred only in the context of this elevated mood episode.

This was followed by a 4-month period characterized by marked reduction in motivation and diminished interest in personal accomplishments, decreased appetite, non-restorative sleep, and low energy interfering with daily tasks. He exhibited psychomotor agitation with restlessness and purposeless movements. He reported excessive and unfounded guilt of a delusional intensity and recurrent suicidal thoughts without a specific plan.

A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Bipolar I Disorder

    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D010_l006.question:
A 28-year-old single male police patrol officer presents with a 2-month history of a markedly elevated and irritable mood accompanied by significant behavioral and functional changes. During this period, he exhibits prominent psychomotor agitation, with an inability to remain still and a persistent drive to stay active. Speech is markedly pressured, rapid, and difficult to interrupt. He describes thoughts as moving excessively fast with frequent shifts between unrelated ideas, consistent with racing thoughts. There is a clear increase in goal-directed activities and a notable escalation in sexual drive and pursuits, representing hypersexual behavior. 

Concomitantly, the patient reports fixed beliefs that neutral events and behaviors of others carry special personal meaning, consistent with referential delusions. He also endorses episodic visual experiences of people or objects that are not actually present. These psychotic symptoms have occurred exclusively during the identified mood elevation and irritability. The symptom cluster has led to significant impairment in occupational functioning and interpersonal interactions, raising concerns regarding his judgment and reliability in his role as a law enforcement officer. There is no indication that demographic factors temporally preceded or precipitated the current episode.

A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Bipolar I Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D010_l007.question:

During this period, she engaged in substantially more work than baseline and initiated multiple projects simultaneously, with associated functional impairment in occupational and social domains.

Marked social disinhibition and increased extroversion were observed, with a notable rise in social interactions and contacting acquaintances well beyond her usual pattern.

Concurrently, she developed fixed, false beliefs that a catastrophic, world-ending event was imminent, despite lack of corroborating evidence, consistent with nihilistic delusional content. She also reported abnormal tactile perceptions of being touched or of movement on her skin in the absence of external stimuli. These psychotic phenomena have occurred exclusively in the context of the described elevated mood state and have not been reported outside this 2-month manic period. No temporally proximate psychosocial stressor was identified as precipitating the current episode.

A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Bipolar I Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D010_l011.question:
